findings.conclusion: Both versions first require CLASS_IN, then test empty entries, then may_have_expired(now). Empty or conservative-live generations yield dotted_name=None. The old helper argument expressions are pure field reads/reborrows; moving these two pure predicates earlier introduces no observable side effect.
Malformed-header rejection and the interface/NXDOMAIN deferral remain before the guard. No additional guard runs on these returns or on non-IN queries.

Same now value and unchanged may_have_expired retain stale-Forever bypass, unknown-bound fallback, negative-time fallback and exact now>=bound threshold. Original fine-grained LeasePolicy.live wrapping arithmetic remains authoritative inside traversal. Active-entry removals stay sticky on clock rollback.

When the guard passes, the entire traversal body is byte-identical: wire_to_dotted failure remains None, up to100 CNAME links, TYPE_CNAME early return, original-name return, PTR/ANY and configured-PTR precedence, has_expired checks and Arc::make_mut calls in the same order. Additional-record expiry path is unchanged.

LeaseView creation and any Arc copy-on-write still precede the same cache.inspect_name/hint assignment. Cached CNAME deferral and single-fresh-address/hint calls remain at identical boundaries with identical dotted_name. Cache generation, validity checks and downstream answer construction are unchanged.

No signature, visibility, caller set, allocation/error-return code or panic branch changes. entries().is_empty and may_have_expired only read LeaseNames fields; inline(never) is the only added compiler attribute.
